title: Five things invented by women
titleChinese: 五件由女性发明的东西
paragraphs: Here‘s a simple challenge: name a famous inventor. Perhaps Renaissance polymath Leonardo da Vinci springs to mind. Or the pioneer of the telephone, Alexander Graham Bell. But you might be hard-pressed to name many female inventors, even though women are behind some of the most widely used technologies in the modern world.

For example, where would we be without the windscreen wiper? Back on a freezing winter’s day in 1902, Mary Anderson was travelling by tram through New York city. Snow was falling, forcing the driver to stop repeatedly and get out to clear it. Each time the door opened, Mary suffered a gust of sub-zero air. She had a brainwave: why not make some kind of a rubber blade that could be operated from inside the vehicle? And that‘s exactly what she did.

Let’s step in from freezing New York for our next invention. The dishwasher dates back even earlier to the 19th Century, and to the dinner parties thrown by a lady called Josephine Cochrane. As a frequent host, she wanted a machine that could wash dishes faster than people. Her response was to develop what was to become the first commercially successful dishwasher.
Interestingly, innovation was in her blood: her grandfather had invented the steamboat.

Need something to do while the dishwasher is whirling away? How about a round of Monopoly? One of the most popular board games around, the rules were first drawn up by a lady called Elizabeth Magie, and patented in 1904. Her intention was to create a game to highlight what she saw as the evils of capitalism. The game was originally called The Landlord‘s Game.
To an altogether different kind of innovation: Kevlar is the lightweight fibre used in bulletproof vests. The material is used by millions every day and has saved countless lives.

The super tough fabric is also used in objects ranging from gloves to aeroplanes to wind turbines. Incredibly, its strength-to-weight ratio is five times higher than steel. Again, it was invented by a woman, the American chemist Stephanie Kwolek, in 1964.

Finally, one of the most important inventions of the 20th Century must surely be the computer programme. The world of programming is notoriously unbalanced in terms of gender. Men vastly outnumber women, and take home around 30% more pay than their female counterparts on average. But back in the 1940s and 50s, women were at the forefront of this new field. Grace Hopper is credited with inventing the first compiler in 1952, which serves as the bridge between code and the binary ones and zeros understood by computers.

vocabulary.entry: polymath [n.] /ˈpɒlɪmæθ/ 博学者；通才 (书面语)
vocabulary.example: Leonardo da Vinci was a renowned polymath.
vocabulary.translation: 列奥纳多·达·芬奇是一位著名的博学者。

vocabulary.entry: spring to mind [phr.] /sprɪŋ tə maɪnd/ 突然想到；立刻想起
vocabulary.example: When I think of great artists, Picasso springs to mind.
vocabulary.translation: 当我想起伟大的艺术家时，立刻想到了毕加索。

vocabulary.entry: be hard-pressed to [phr.] /biː ˌhɑːd ˈprest tuː/ 很难；难以
vocabulary.example: You‘d be hard-pressed to find a better restaurant.
vocabulary.translation: 你很难找到一家更好的餐厅。

vocabulary.entry: date back to [phr.] /deɪt bæk tuː/ 追溯到；始于
vocabulary.example: This tradition dates back to the 15th century.
vocabulary.translation: 这个传统可以追溯到15世纪。

vocabulary.entry: throw a party [phr.] /θrəʊ ə ˈpɑːti/ 举办聚会；举行派对 (口语)
vocabulary.example: They threw a party to celebrate their anniversary.
vocabulary.translation: 他们举办了一个派对来庆祝结婚纪念日。

vocabulary.entry: draw up [phr.] /drɔː ʌp/ 起草；拟定
vocabulary.example: The lawyers drew up a contract.
vocabulary.translation: 律师们拟定了一份合同。

vocabulary.entry: be credited with [phr.] /biː ˈkredɪtɪd wɪð/ 被认为是……的功劳；因……而受到称赞
vocabulary.example: She is credited with discovering the new species.
vocabulary.translation: 她被认为是发现这个新物种的人。

vocabulary.entry: serve as [phr.] /sɜːv æz/ 担任；充当；用作
vocabulary.example: The sofa serves as a bed for guests.
vocabulary.translation: 这张沙发用作客人的床。

vocabulary.entry: in terms of [phr.] /ɪn tɜːmz əv/ 就……而言；从……方面来说
vocabulary.example: In terms of price, this is a good deal.
vocabulary.translation: 就价格而言，这笔交易很划算。

vocabulary.entry: outnumber [v.] /aʊtˈnʌmbə/ 在数量上超过；比……多
vocabulary.example: In this class, girls outnumber boys.
vocabulary.translation: 这个班级里女生人数超过男生。

vocabulary.entry: at the forefront of [phr.] /æt ðə ˈfɔːfrʌnt əv/ 处于……的前沿；在前列
vocabulary.example: The company is at the forefront of green technology.
vocabulary.translation: 这家公司处于绿色技术的前沿。

vocabulary.entry: take home [phr.] /teɪk həʊm/ 挣得；获得（薪水）(口语)
vocabulary.example: She takes home $50,000 a year.
vocabulary.translation: 她每年挣5万美元。

vocabulary.entry: wind turbine [n.] /ˈwɪnd tɜːbaɪn/ 风力涡轮机；风力发电机
vocabulary.example: Wind turbines generate clean energy.
vocabulary.translation: 风力涡轮机产生清洁能源。

vocabulary.entry: be behind [phr.] /biː bɪˈhaɪnd/ 是……的背后原因；支持
vocabulary.example: Who is behind this new project?
vocabulary.translation: 谁是这项新项目的幕后推动者？

vocabulary.entry: sub-zero [adj.] /ˌsʌb ˈzɪərəʊ/ 零下的；低于零度的
vocabulary.example: Temperatures are expected to drop to sub-zero tonight.
vocabulary.translation: 预计今晚气温将降至零度以下。

vocabulary.entry: a gust of [phr.] /ə ɡʌst əv/ 一阵（风、雨等）
vocabulary.example: A gust of wind blew the papers off the desk.
vocabulary.translation: 一阵风把文件从桌子上吹落了。

vocabulary.entry: windscreen wiper [n.] /ˈwɪndskriːn ˈwaɪpə/ 挡风玻璃雨刷 (英式英语)
vocabulary.example: Turn on the windscreen wipers when it rains.
vocabulary.translation: 下雨时打开挡风玻璃雨刷。

vocabulary.entry: brainwave [n.] /ˈbreɪnweɪv/ 灵感；妙计 (口语)
vocabulary.example: He had a brainwave and solved the problem instantly.
vocabulary.translation: 他灵机一动，立刻解决了问题。

vocabulary.entry: bulletproof vest [n.] /ˈbʊlɪtpruːf vest/ 防弹背心
vocabulary.example: Police officers wear bulletproof vests for protection.
vocabulary.translation: 警察穿防弹背心以作保护。

vocabulary.entry: compiler [n.] /kəmˈpaɪlə/ 编译器 (计算机术语)
vocabulary.example: The compiler translates code into machine language.
vocabulary.translation: 编译器将代码翻译成机器语言。
